stories.title: US formally ends military presence in Iraq
stories.details: The United States has officially withdrawn its last remaining soldiers from Iraq, marking the end of a two-decade military commitment. The departure follows years of instability, including the rise of insurgencies and the influence of regional powers like Iran, leaving behind a nation still grappling with the consequences of the 2003 invasion.

stories.title: No 10 gathering evidence on public support for UK rejoining EU
stories.details: Downing Street officials have begun reaching out to thinktanks and pollsters to gauge public sentiment regarding a potential reversal of Brexit. The move suggests the government is testing the political viability of rejoining the European Union.

stories.title: UK suspects Iranian role in RAF Fairford incident
stories.details: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has stated there are strong indications that Iran played a role in a recent security incident at the RAF Fairford air base. The government is investigating the extent of foreign interference in the security breach.

stories.title: Drumcree standoff continues in Northern Ireland
stories.details: The Orange Order has refused to accept a proposed deal regarding the Drumcree standoff, stating they will not surrender. The situation remains tense as negotiations between the group and authorities continue without a resolution.

stories.title: New Google Maps images reveal devastation in Gaza
stories.details: Updated satellite imagery from Google Maps has highlighted the massive scale of destruction across Gaza following the ongoing conflict. The visuals provide a stark look at the physical toll the war has taken on the region's infrastructure.

title: The Silicon Frontier: AI Regulation and the New Global Arms Race

stories.title: US trade regulator opens investigation into AI giants
stories.details: The US trade regulator has launched a formal investigation into major AI companies, including Anthropic and OpenAI. The probe is expected to examine the competitive practices and development standards of these industry leaders.

stories.title: OpenAI launches 'Dots' assistant
stories.details: OpenAI has introduced 'Dots,' an always-on personal assistant powered by GPT-6 Astra. Designed to compete with Meta's Muse agent, the tool operates independently of specific interfaces to help users achieve goals.

stories.title: Trump releases voluntary AI accord
stories.details: Donald Trump has announced a voluntary agreement with six major tech companies, including Google and Nvidia, to implement safety safeguards for advanced AI. The accord focuses on independent auditing and cybersecurity, though it currently lacks legal enforcement.

stories.title: DeepSeek and Huawei partner on AI chip software
stories.details: DeepSeek has teamed up with Huawei to develop open-source programming tools for Huawei's Ascend AI chips. The collaboration aims to reduce reliance on Nvidia's hardware by optimizing software for domestic Chinese chips.

title: UK Economic Pulse: Housing, Incomes, and Retail Restructuring

stories.title: Annual UK house price growth halves
stories.details: Nationwide reports that annual UK house price growth has slowed to 0.8%, the weakest rate since late 2025. The cooling market is attributed to rising mortgage rates and broader economic uncertainty.

stories.title: UK income growth revised upwards
stories.details: Official data shows UK income growth has been revised higher, with markets describing the economy as resilient. The positive revision comes despite broader concerns about inflation and interest rate pressures.

stories.title: Greggs to shut four factories
stories.details: Greggs has announced a restructuring plan that involves closing four UK factories. The move puts approximately 740 jobs at risk as the bakery chain looks to optimize its manufacturing operations.

stories.title: Poundland management in talks for rescue bid
stories.details: Management at Poundland is currently in negotiations to lead a bid that could potentially save 11,000 jobs. The move comes as the retail sector faces ongoing financial pressures.

title: Global Perspectives: Aviation Security, Tactical Shifts, and Cricket Diplomacy

stories.title: Pilot attacked on Dubai-to-Israel flight
stories.details: A Flydubai flight to Israel was diverted after the co-pilot allegedly attacked the captain in a suspected terror attempt. Passengers and off-duty pilots intervened to storm the cockpit and regain control of the aircraft.

stories.title: Bellingham a striking alternative for England
stories.details: England manager Thomas Tuchel has praised Jude Bellingham's versatility, suggesting he could serve as a striking alternative in the No 9 role. The tactical shift is being considered as England prepares for upcoming international fixtures.

stories.title: ECB to allow England cricketers in Afghanistan Premier League
stories.details: The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) is set to permit two centrally contracted players to participate in the Afghanistan Premier League. This decision comes despite the board's ongoing refusal to play bilateral series against the country.

title: The Shadow Over the Etihad: Guardiola, Governance, and the Future of Manchester City

stories.title: Barney Ronay on the 'Pep supremacy'
stories.details: Football critic Barney Ronay argues that the era of Manchester City's dominance under Pep Guardiola will be defined by the controversy surrounding the club's alleged financial breaches. He characterizes the current state of play as 'sham-ball'.

stories.title: Andy Burnham concerned over Man City ownership
stories.details: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has expressed concern regarding the potential loss of Manchester City's owners should the club be found guilty of over 100 breaches of Premier League rules. He emphasized the importance of the club to the local economy.
